issues.t: Stability control may brake or cut power unexpectedly
issues.sym: The vehicle brakes on its own or loses power for a moment, often with the ESC light flashing.
issues.why: The yaw rate sensor used by stability control was too sensitive and could trigger braking or cut engine power when it was not needed. Hyundai reprogrammed the control unit.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls and have the update done before regular driving.

issues.t: Parking brake may not hold
issues.sym: The parking brake lever does not click and hold, or it releases on its own.
issues.why: Ratchet teeth in the parking brake lever could be damaged, so the brake may not engage or may let go, and the vehicle could roll.
issues.next: Park in gear on level ground and check the VIN for the recalls. Get the lever replaced.

issues.t: Driver air bag protection for small occupants
issues.sym: No symptom. The issue only shows in certain frontal crashes.
issues.why: The driver air bag did not give enough protection margin for small unbelted adults in some crashes. Hyundai replaced the air bag module.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recalls and always wear the seat belt.

issues.t: Brake light switch failure
issues.sym: Brake lights do not come on or stay on, the shifter will not come out of Park, cruise control acts up, or the ESC light comes on.
issues.why: The brake lamp switch could malfunction. Hyundai replaced the switch under several recalls.
issues.next: Have someone check your brake lights. If they do not work, get the switch replaced before driving in traffic.

issues.t: Harsh or delayed shifts and solenoid codes
issues.sym: A hard clunk going into Drive or Reverse, late or harsh shifts, slipping, or a check-engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: Hyundai released several bulletins for harsh engagement, shift solenoid and speed sensor codes on this automatic, and owners report slipping and replacements.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask about the shift-quality bulletins and software updates. Fix slipping early to avoid a full rebuild.

issues.t: Lean running codes from air filter housing
issues.sym: A check-engine light with lean codes P0171 or P0174, sometimes with a slight hesitation.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin tying these codes to the air filter housing letting unmeasured air into the engine.
issues.next: Have a shop check the air filter housing and intake for leaks before replacing sensors.

issues.t: Oil leak between transaxle and transfer case
issues.sym: Oil drips or wetness where the transmission meets the transfer case on AWD models.
issues.why: Hyundai issued a bulletin for a seal leak at the joint between the transaxle and transfer case.
issues.next: Have the leak checked and the seal replaced, and keep the fluid topped up.

issues.t: No start in freezing weather from exhaust
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start on very cold mornings.
issues.why: Water in the exhaust pipe could freeze and block it. Hyundai issued a bulletin to replace the exhaust pipe.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the bulletin if your Tucson struggles to start in freezing weather.

issues.t: Passenger air bag sensor misreads occupant
issues.sym: The passenger air bag warning lamp comes on with a heavier adult in the seat.
issues.why: The occupant sensor could misjudge who is in the seat, and could leave the air bag active for a child. Hyundai reprogrammed the module.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and keep children in the back seat.

issues.t: Rough shifting and transmission temperature codes
issues.sym: Jerky or delayed shifts, slipping, a check-engine light with P0711 or P0713, or the vehicle not moving after a stop.
issues.why: Owners report shift problems on this automatic, and Hyundai issued a bulletin for the fluid temperature sensor and wiring.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask about bulletin 11-AT-010 and any software updates. Stop driving if the vehicle will not move or slips badly.

issues.t: Transmission cooler hose may leak
issues.sym: Red fluid under the front of the vehicle, a burning smell, or the transmission losing drive.
issues.why: A transmission fluid cooler hose could leak. Fluid on hot parts is a fire risk, and losing fluid can ruin the transmission.
issues.next: Do not drive if fluid is leaking. Check the VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Engine knock and bearing wear
issues.sym: Knocking or ticking that gets louder, oil use, metal in the oil, a check-engine light, or sudden power loss or stalling.
issues.why: Engines from this era can wear their connecting rod bearings. Hyundai added knock-monitoring software and extended engine coverage on many vehicles.
issues.next: Check the oil level often, ask a dealer about campaign 953 and any extended engine coverage for your VIN, and stop driving if a knock appears.

issues.t: Engine oil pan may leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the engine, a low oil level, or the oil pressure light coming on.
issues.why: The oil pan could leak and let the engine run low on oil, which can destroy it. Hyundai inspected or replaced the pan and updated the oil pressure switch.
issues.next: Check the oil now and stop driving if the oil light comes on. Get the recall done.

issues.t: ABS control module fire risk
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from under the hood, possibly with the ABS light on, even while parked.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake module can leak fluid internally and short circuit. Hyundai recalled these years and told owners to park outside.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and park outdoors, away from buildings, until it is repaired.

issues.t: Steering wheel air bag may come loose
issues.sym: The center of the steering wheel feels loose or rattles, or the air bag light is on.
issues.why: Bolts holding the driver air bag to the steering wheel could loosen, so it may not deploy correctly.
issues.next: Get the recall done promptly so the bolts are tightened.

issues.t: Dual-clutch transmission hesitation and shudder
issues.sym: Hesitation or a brief loss of drive when pulling away, shuddering or jerking at low speeds, or a transmission overheat warning in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: The dry dual-clutch transmission had control software and clutch wear problems. Hyundai issued a software recall and bulletins that adjust for clutch wear.
issues.next: Check for open recalls and ask a dealer about the latest transmission software. Be careful pulling into traffic until it is resolved.

issues.t: ABS control module fire risk
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay, possibly with an ABS warning.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control unit can corrode inside and short circuit. It was recalled with advice to park outside.
issues.next: Run a VIN recall check and keep the vehicle parked outside until it is repaired.

issues.t: Engine bearing wear and knocking
issues.sym: Knocking or ticking, burning oil, a check-engine light, stalling, or a sudden loss of power.
issues.why: These years draw many engine-failure complaints, and Hyundai recalled certain 2017 models because connecting rod bearings could wear early.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly, look up open recalls for your VIN, and stop driving if a knock appears.

issues.t: Hood secondary latch may not hold
issues.sym: The hood can lift after the inside release is pulled, or pop up while driving.
issues.why: The secondary hood latch could fail to hold the hood once the main latch was released.
issues.next: Make sure the hood is fully closed before driving and get the latch replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Trailer hitch wiring keeps brake lights on
issues.sym: Trailer brake lights stay on, or trailer turn signals do not flash, with the accessory hitch harness.
issues.why: The accessory trailer wiring harness had faults that affected trailer lights. Hyundai replaced or updated the harness.
issues.next: Check trailer lights before towing and ask a dealer about the harness recalls.

issues.t: Tow hitch wiring module can short and burn
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke near the rear, or trailer lights not working.
issues.why: Water can get into the optional tow hitch wiring module and short it, which can start a fire. Hyundai told owners to park outside.
issues.next: Park outside, away from buildings, and get the recall repair. Do not tow until it is fixed.

issues.t: Idle stop oil pump controller can overheat
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke, or warning lights, often after the engine shuts off at stops.
issues.why: The controller for the electric oil pump that supports Idle Stop and Go can overheat and start a fire. Hyundai told owners to park outside.
issues.next: Park outside until the controller is replaced under the recall.

issues.t: Roof moldings may come off
issues.sym: Wind noise, flapping, or a loose roof trim strip.
issues.why: Roof moldings could detach while driving and become a hazard to other drivers.
issues.next: Have the moldings inspected and secured under the recall.

issues.t: Loss of power steering assist
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets heavy, often with a steering warning light.
issues.why: A circuit board in the power steering unit can short and shut off the assist.
issues.next: Get the recall done promptly. If assist is lost, slow down and drive carefully to a safe stop.

issues.t: Can shift out of Park without the brake
issues.sym: The shifter comes out of Park without pressing the brake pedal.
issues.why: Wiring in the center console could let the shift lock be bypassed.
issues.next: Keep your foot on the brake when shifting and get the wiring rerouted under the recall.

issues.t: Connecting rod bolts may be under-tightened
issues.sym: Engine knocking, an oil leak, a check-engine light, or loss of power.
issues.why: Some engines were built with connecting rod bolts not tightened enough, which can lead to engine damage. Hyundai is replacing affected engines.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and stop driving if you hear knocking or lose power.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark or freezes, hiding speed and warning lights.
issues.why: A software error in the instrument cluster can make the display fail. Hyundai fixes it over the air or at the dealer.
issues.next: Accept the over-the-air update or visit a dealer. Drive carefully if gauges are not showing.

issues.t: Unexpected automatic emergency braking
issues.sym: The vehicle brakes hard by itself when nothing is in the way.
issues.why: Software for the front camera used by collision avoidance can falsely detect an obstacle.
issues.next: Get the dealer software update promptly and watch traffic behind you.

issues.t: Side curtain air bags may be installed wrong
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The air bag light may come on.
issues.why: The curtain air bags may not have been installed properly, which can affect protection in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the air bags reinstalled.

issues.t: Side impact sensor may be misassembled
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The air bag light may come on.
issues.why: A side impact sensor in the center pillar may be assembled wrong, which could delay air bag deployment in a side crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the sensor inspected.
